options: The postal address of a customer
The geographic location, expressed as an exact position on Earth
The country code of a telephone number
The time zone of a transaction
The IP address of a device
questions.explanation: Geocoding refers to the geographic location: not merely name, street, city or region but the exact location on Earth.

questions.stem: Which data elements exactly represent Geocoding?
options: Longitude and Latitude, also known as Lat and Long
questions.explanation: The exact data elements representing Geocoding are Longitude and Latitude, commonly known as Lat and Long.

questions.stem: What can one do using Lat and Long?
options: Reach the exact location anywhere in the world
questions.explanation: Using latitude and longitude one can reach the exact location anywhere in the world.

questions.stem: Why has location information become so important in the current era?
options: Because databases require it as a primary key
Because social media, mobile applications, sensors, satellite scans and CCTV have become the norm and millions use mobiles everywhere, all the time
Because it is cheaper to store than addresses
questions.explanation: With data generated everywhere by everyone through mobiles, sensors, satellites and CCTV, location has become one of the most important pieces of information, especially about consumers.

questions.stem: In the Amazon example, what could Amazon not do without knowing where buyers are located?
questions.explanation: If Amazon does not know where buyers are and where most buyers of a product are located, it cannot plan its marketing campaigns.

questions.stem: According to *I Am Datapedia!*, to whom does Amazon sell data about which products are bought from which locations?
questions.explanation: Amazon sells location-based buying data to production houses so they can plan production and relocate stock.

questions.stem: How do production houses use location-based buying data?
options: To plan their next production or relocate products from low-demand to high-demand locations
questions.explanation: Production houses use the data to plan production and to move products from less in-demand locations to high in-demand locations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT named among the modern sources that have made location data ubiquitous?
questions.explanation: Social media, mobile applications, sensors, satellite scans, CCTV and online video and audio are named; floppy drives belong to the Data Island discussion.

questions.stem: Which statement about Geocoding is correct?
options: It is about the exact location on Earth rather than just name, street, city or region
It is only about the name of a city or region
It requires a postal address to work
It is unrelated to consumer data
It is only used by satellite operators
questions.explanation: Geocoding is about the exact position on Earth, represented by latitude and longitude, rather than a descriptive address.

questions.stem: How is Amazon characterised in the Geocoding example?
options: One of the most used online stores worldwide, used by millions to buy and sell products 24/7
questions.explanation: Amazon is described as one of the most used online stores around the globe, used by millions of people to buy and sell products 24/7.
